issues.claim: the console provider, for example, prints the full exception text with the stack trace and inner exceptions below the message
issues.problem: This is true: the simple console formatter writes exception.ToString() after the message. However, none of the supplied link excerpts shows it, and the generator flagged it as from memory. The same sentence exists in ru.

issues.claim: Посмотрите на сигнатуру `ILogger.Log`. Есть ли у неё отдельный параметр для исключения, и какой из вызовов его заполняет?
issues.problem: The hint is acceptable but points very close to the answer. It nearly states that the overload taking the exception fills the parameter. The EN hint is the same.
issues.suggestedFix: Weaken to: "Подумайте, какую информацию о сбое получает провайдер: только текст сообщения или что-то ещё?" (EN: "Think about what the provider receives: only the message text, or something more?")

issues.claim: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/standard/exceptions/best-practices-for-exceptions (cited for the two-pass order filter, finally, catch)
issues.problem: The fetched excerpt covers try/catch/finally and cleanup. It says nothing about exception filters, two-pass dispatch or the order of filter versus nested finally. It does not support the claim at the core of the question.
issues.suggestedFix: Replace this link with a source that describes two-pass dispatch, for example the CoreCLR Book of the Runtime exception handling page https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/docs/design/coreclr/botr/exceptions.md (kind: article) or ECMA-335 Partition I, exception handling (kind: spec). Update linkTitles in both locales.

issues.claim: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/language-reference/statements/exception-handling-statements (cited for filter running before inner finally, and for locks and using resources still being held)
issues.problem: The excerpt supports only that a `when` filter does not unwind the stack and preserves the stack trace. It does not state that filters run before finally blocks of nested frames, nor that inner locks and using resources are still held while the filter runs. These are consequences of two-pass dispatch that the generator itself says are not quoted from a source. The sandbox confirms the output, but the explanation is not backed by a cited source.
issues.suggestedFix: Keep this link for "the filter does not unwind the stack", and add the BOTR or ECMA-335 source for the two-pass claim. Phrase the lock and using point as a consequence, as the text already does.

issues.claim: When does the runtime find out which `catch` will handle the exception - before the stack is unwound or while it is being unwound?
issues.problem: The hint nearly gives away the hinge: it says the handler is found before unwinding, and from that the order follows. The RU hint has the same strength.
issues.suggestedFix: Soften to: "Which runs first: evaluating the `when` condition, or the cleanup code of the frames the exception passes through?" (RU equivalent: "Что выполняется раньше: вычисление условия `when` или код очистки в кадрах, через которые проходит исключение?")
